title: A Model for Pediatric Healthcare Networks in Germany
summary:
Background
Children and adolescents sometimes require care from different physicians, hospitals, and other healthcare providers. To ensure that care is well coordinated, many of these providers work together within healthcare networks.

The **Vernetzt4Kids** project aims to identify the factors that contribute to successful healthcare networks and to explore how collaboration can be further improved. To achieve this, we are interested in the experiences and perspectives of families, patients, and healthcare professionals.

The findings of this study will help improve healthcare services for children and adolescents in Germany and facilitate access to specialized care.

Study Objective
The objective of this study is to better understand how collaboration between pediatric hospitals, office-based pediatricians, and other healthcare providers can be organized to ensure the best possible care for children and adolescents. We aim to identify factors that contribute to successful collaboration as well as challenges that may hinder effective networking.

Study Procedures
As part of the project, information from various sources will be collected and analyzed. This includes surveys of caregivers, patients, and healthcare professionals. In addition, existing experiences and results from four established healthcare networks ("Sichere Geburt", "KidS", "RTP-Net", and "PIN") will be evaluated.

The knowledge gained from these activities will be used to develop recommendations for the further improvement of healthcare services and healthcare networks for children and adolescents.
conditions: Pediatric Healthcare Networks as a Healthcare Delivery Structure

interventions.name: Analysis of four regional pediatric healthcare networks: the maternity and perinatal care network “Sichere Geburt” (Safe Birth), the “Kinderteleintensivnetzwerk Sachsen” (KidS; Pediatric Tele-Intensive Care Network Saxony), the “Pädiatrisches Intensivnetzwerk” (PIN; Pediatric Intensive Care Network)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Study Component: Interviews with Network Staff
It is intended that all participating healthcare networks are represented among the interview participants.

Study Component: Survey of Caregivers
Eligible participants are caregivers of pediatric patients who are currently receiving or have previously received care at one of the participating network hospitals (including all hospitals affiliated with the respective networks).

Study Component: Survey of Office-Based Pediatricians
The survey targets office-based pediatricians throughout Germany who provide care for pediatric patients.

Study Component: Workshops with Patients and Caregivers
Eligible participants are patients aged 16 to 18 years and caregivers of patients who have received care at a hospital affiliated with one of the four participating networks.
Participants of the first workshop round will be invited and encouraged to participate in the second workshop round to ensure continuity and facilitate the further development and validation of the project results.
Exclusion criteria:
Missing informed consent
